title: How to choose a B2B support platform: Features, framework, fit | Pylon
summary: Choosing a B2B support platform? Compare account-centric features, follow a step-by-step evaluation framework, and pick software built to scale.
body_markdown:
*Updated July 10, 2026 | 25 min read*


## TL;DR


Choosing the right B2B support platform means understanding the differences between B2B and B2C support.


B2B support platforms should be able to:


- handle complex account relationships with multiple stakeholders
- support communication across channels like Slack, Teams, Discord, and email
- provide deep insights into account health


Key features to look for include:


- account-centric support models
- support for omnichannel communication
- SLA management
- integrations with your existing tech stack


Research shows that companies that use modern B2B support platforms achieve 315% ROI over three years with sub-six-month payback periods. And increasing customer retention rates by 5% can boost profits by 25-95%.


## What Makes B2B Support Platforms Different from B2C Tools?


B2B customer support operates in a fundamentally different environment than B2C support. While B2C teams focus on resolving high volumes of customer transactions, B2B support teams manage complex, long-term relationships and contract renewals.


### The Core Differences


**Multiple Stakeholders Per Account**


Unlike B2C support where you generally help one person at a time, B2B support involves coordinating with multiple decision-makers from the same organization. In fact, 63% of B2B deals involve more than four decision-makers. Each stakeholder brings unique concerns:


- Technical users need product specifications and integration details
- Managers focus on return on investment
- Procurement teams evaluate contract terms
- End users care about usability and training


Your support platform needs to track all these relationships under a unified account view, rather than treating each person as an isolated support ticket.


**Longer, More Complex Customer Journeys**


B2B sales cycles can last from one month to over a year, and support interactions mirror this complexity. What starts as a simple question could evolve into a multi-week technical implementation that requires coordination between your support, engineering, and customer success teams.


Traditional ticketing systems designed for quick B2C resolutions break down when they try to handle these extended, multi-phase interactions. You need a platform built for relationship management, not just issue resolution.


**Higher Stakes and Urgency**


When a B2B customer experiences an issue, it doesn't just affect one person—it can disrupt entire organizations. Poor B2B customer support can damage a company's reputation and lead to lost deals.


**Business Communication Channels**


B2B customers don't want to leave their workflow to get support. They expect help through the communication platforms they already use, like Slack Connect, Microsoft Teams, Discord, and customer portals—not just email and web forms.


According to[reports on modern business communication](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/practical-guide-to-omnichannel-support) , companies that meet customers on their preferred channels see significantly higher satisfaction scores and faster resolution times.


## Key Features That Define Modern B2B Support Platforms


To help you evaluate B2B support platforms effectively, you need to understand which capabilities really count. The following features directly address the unique challenges of B2B support.


### 1. Account-Centric Support Architecture


The fundamental difference between B2C and B2B support platforms is how they organize customer information. Consumer tools focus on individual users and tickets. B2B platforms focus on accounts.


What account-centric support provides:


- Unified view of all tickets, conversations, and interactions across every stakeholder at an account
- Account health metrics and risk indicators surfaced automatically
- Historical context that helps support teams understand the full relationship
- Ability to track SLAs, renewal dates, and contract details at the account level


When evaluating platforms, test how easily you can see the complete picture of an account's support history, contract status, and health metrics in a single place.


### 2. Native Business Messaging Integration


Many support platforms now offer omnichannel integrations. But there's a crucial distinction: notification-based integrations vs. native support experiences.


**Notification-based integrations** simply alert agents in Slack or Teams when tickets arrive in another system. Support teams still need to context-switch to respond.


**Native integrations** let customers raise, discuss, and resolve issues entirely within Slack, Teams, or Discord without leaving their workspace. The support platform is invisible to the customer while giving support teams full ticketing capabilities behind the scenes.


For B2B companies, native integration is essential. If your customers mainly use Slack Connect or Microsoft Teams for vendor communication, forcing them to switch to email or a web portal creates unnecessary friction.


Learn more about implementing effective[Slack integrations for customer support](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/slack-integrations-customer-support-2025) and[Discord for customer support](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/discord-for-customer-support-guide-2025) .


### 3. Multi-Product and Service Tier Management


B2B companies often serve customers across multiple products or service tiers under a single account. Your support platform needs to handle this complexity well.


Essential capabilities:


- Tag and categorize issues by product or service tier
- Route tickets to specialized teams based on product expertise
- Track SLAs and metrics separately for different product or service offerings
- Provide support teams with product-specific knowledge bases and documentation
- Generate reports segmented by product or service


This becomes especially important as your business grows. A platform that treats your entire catalog as a monolithic offering will create bottlenecks and confusion as you scale.


### 4. SLA Management and Compliance Tracking


Service Level Agreements (SLAs) define your contractual obligations to B2B customers. Your platform should help you meet those commitments consistently.


Critical SLA features:


- Automatic SLA assignment based on account tier, issue priority, or product
- Real-time alerts when tickets approach SLA breach
- Escalation workflows triggered by time-based rules
- Comprehensive reporting on SLA compliance rates
- Separate SLA tracks for different response types (first response, resolution, update frequency)


Look for platforms that make SLA compliance proactive rather than reactive. The best systems alert your team before breaches occur and automatically escalate when needed.


### 5. Knowledge Management and Self-Service


Helping customers solve issues independently reduces your team’s ticket volume and improves satisfaction. Research shows 78% of customers prefer to solve issues by themselves through self-service.


Modern knowledge base requirements:


- Easy content creation and maintenance by non-technical team members
- AI-powered search that understands natural language queries
- Version control and approval workflows for content updates
- Analytics showing which articles are most helpful and where gaps exist
- Integration with your support channels so your team can share articles instantly


The best platforms treat the knowledge base as a core feature rather than an afterthought. When you’re evaluating platforms, pay attention to how easy it is to create, organize, and surface relevant knowledge base content.


Read more about[knowledge base platform options](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/knowledge-base-software-2025) and[best practices for creating B2B knowledge bases](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/best-practices-for-creating-a-b2b-knowledge-base) .


### 6. AI-Powered Automation and Intelligence


AI has evolved from a buzzword to a practical necessity in modern support operations. HubSpot's 2024 State of Service Report shows 92% of CRM leaders say AI has improved response times, and 77% believed AI would handle most tickets by 2025.


Practical AI applications in B2B support:


- Automatic ticket triage and routing based on content, urgency, and account value
- Response suggestions that support teams can edit and send, maintaining accuracy while increasing speed
- Sentiment analysis to flag frustrated customers before escalation
- Automatic summarization of long conversation threads
- Proactive identification of at-risk accounts based on support patterns


The key is AI that boosts your support team rather than trying to replace them. B2B issues often require nuanced understanding and relationship context that pure automation can’t provide.


[Learn how to implement AI-powered customer support](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/ai-powered-customer-support-guide) effectively in your organization.


### 7. Cross-Team Collaboration Tools


B2B support doesn’t happen in isolation. Resolving complex issues requires coordination between support teams, customer success managers, product teams, and engineering.


Essential collaboration features:


- Internal notes and conversations attached to tickets
- @mentions to pull in specific team members
- Shared issues views across teams
- Integration with project management and development tools (Jira, Linear, GitHub)
- Smooth handoffs between support and customer success teams


When you evaluate support platforms, involve folks from all the teams that will use the product. A platform that works well for your support team but creates friction for engineering or customer success will ultimately slow down issue resolution.


### 8. Deep Integration Capabilities


Your support platform needs to connect seamlessly with your existing tools to give your teams complete context.


Critical integrations:


- **CRM systems** (Salesforce, HubSpot) for account data, contract information, and opportunity tracking
- **Communication platforms** (Slack, Teams, Discord) for omnichannel support experiences
- **Project management and development tools** (Jira, Linear, GitHub) for technical issue tracking and escalation
- **Data warehouses** (Snowflake, BigQuery) for custom reporting and analytics


Don't just check if these integrations exist; test how well they connect. Can your team see relevant CRM data without leaving the support platform? Can they create engineering tickets with one click?


### 9. Advanced Analytics and Reporting


B2B support drives business outcomes, and you need data to prove it. Basic metrics like ticket volume and response time don't tell the full story.


Strategic metrics B2B platforms should track:


- Account health scores based on customer conversations and issues
- Time to resolution segmented by issue type, product, and customer tier
- AI agent productivity and quality metrics
- Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) and Net Promoter Score (NPS) trends
- Support's impact on renewal rates and expansion revenue
- Cost per ticket and support efficiency ratios


The best platforms make it easy to create custom reports and dashboards without data science expertise. Look for the ability to export data for deeper analysis.


For more on measuring support effectiveness, read about[13 customer support KPIs B2B businesses need to track](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/13-customer-support-kpis-b2b-businesses-need-to-track) .


### 10. Enterprise Security and Compliance


B2B customers, especially in regulated industries, need strict security standards and compliance certifications.


Non-negotiable security requirements:


- SOC 2 Type II compliance at minimum
- GDPR compliance for European customers
- Role-based access controls and permissions
- Data encryption in transit and at rest
- Single sign-on (SSO) support
- Audit logs for all system access and changes


Smaller companies might overlook security early on, but it becomes a dealbreaker as you move upmarket. Choose a platform that meets enterprise security standards so it scales with you.


## How B2B Platforms Support Long-Term Account Health


The most sophisticated B2B support platforms do more than resolve tickets—they actively contribute to account health and retention.


### Proactive Issue Detection


Modern platforms analyze support patterns to identify problems before they escalate:


- Increased ticket volume from a normally quiet account signals potential issues
- Sentiment analysis flags frustrated customers
- Unresolved tickets that are approaching critical timelines trigger escalation
- Product usage data combined with support history predicts churn risk


Companies that invest in advanced customer support platforms can improve response times, reduce costs, and increase customer satisfaction.


### Account Health Scoring


Leading platforms calculate account health scores by combining multiple signals:


- Support ticket frequency and severity
- Customer satisfaction survey responses
- Product adoption and usage metrics
- Contract renewal proximity
- Time since last positive interaction


These scores help customer success teams prioritize outreach and intervention, ensuring high-value accounts receive proactive attention before problems become critical.


[Pylon’s Account Intelligence](https://www.usepylon.com/account-intelligence) can help you pull scattered signals across customer conversations and issues into one place to calculate health scores and identify churn risk.


### Customer Success Integration


Customer support and success work closely in the B2B space. The best platforms facilitate seamless collaboration:


- Automatic alerts to customer success managers when support issues indicate broader adoption challenges
- Shared visibility into both support tickets and success milestones
- Coordinated communication so customers don't receive conflicting messages
- Success playbooks triggered by support patterns (e.g., intensive onboarding support triggers proactive training outreach)


This integrated approach transforms support from a reactive cost center into a strategic function that drives retention and expansion revenue.


### Lifecycle-Based Support Workflows


Different stages of the customer lifecycle require different support approaches:


Onboarding (days 0-90):


- Higher touch support with faster response times
- Proactive outreach to ensure successful implementation
- Training resources and documentation emphasis
- Success metrics tracking to identify struggling customers


Steady state (ongoing):


- Efficient ticket resolution within standard SLAs
- Self-service enablement to reduce ticket volume
- Proactive communication about product updates and new features
- Regular health checks and business reviews


Renewal period (60-90 days before contract end):


- Expedited support for any outstanding issues
- Executive escalation paths for critical accounts
- Documentation of support excellence for renewal conversations
- Proactive outreach to address any concerns


Expansion opportunities:


- Identification of accounts ready for upsell based on support patterns
- Coordination with sales teams when support interactions reveal expansion potential
- Case studies and references from satisfied customers


Your platform should support these different workflows through automation rules, custom views, and flexible SLA configurations.


For additional strategies,[explore B2B customer service best practices](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/b2b-customer-service-best-practices-strategies) .


## How to Evaluate B2B Support Platforms: A Step-by-Step Framework


With so many support platforms to choose from, you need a systematic approach to identify the right fit.


### Step 1: Define Your Requirements


Before scheduling demos, document your specific needs:


Current state assessment:


- What is your support team’s capacity like right now? How about projected in 12 months?
- What's your current monthly ticket volume?
- Which communication channels do your customers prefer?
- What percentage of your tickets require escalation to engineering or product teams?
- What are your average response and resolution times?
- What's causing the most pain in your current system?


Future state vision:


- What customer experience do you want to deliver?
- How will support scale as your company grows?
- What metrics will define success?
- Which integrations are must-haves and which are nice-to-haves?


Budget and timeline:


- What's your budget for a support platform?
- How quickly do you need to implement?
- Do you have technical resources for complex implementation?


### Step 2: Create Your Shortlist


Based on your requirements, identify 3-5 platforms to evaluate seriously.


Evaluation criteria:


1. **Core B2B capabilities** (account management, multi-stakeholder support, SLA management)
2. **Communication channel support** (native integration with your customers' preferred platforms)
3. **Integration ecosystem** (connections to your existing tech stack)
4. **Pricing model** (does it scale reasonably as you grow?)
5. **Company trajectory** (is the vendor investing in product development?)


Research review sites like G2 and Capterra, but take reviews in context: Different companies have differing needs. Pay special attention to reviews from companies similar to yours in size, industry, and customer profile.


If you're considering traditional help desk platforms,[review Zendesk alternatives](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/14-best-zendesk-alternatives-competitors) to understand the modern landscape.


### Step 3: Test with Real Scenarios


During demos and trials, don't settle for generic walk-throughs. Test the platforms with scenarios from your actual support work:


Multi-stakeholder account:


- Create a demo account with multiple contacts
- Submit tickets from different stakeholders
- Evaluate how easily your team can see complete account context
- Check if you can track conversations and resolutions across all customers


Complex technical issue:


- Create a ticket that requires escalation to engineering
- Test the handoff workflow and internal collaboration tools
- Verify that context doesn't get lost during escalation
- Check how easily engineering can update customers on progress


SLA compliance:


- Set up different SLA tiers for test accounts
- Verify that your support team receives appropriate alerts
- Test escalation rules when tickets approach SLA breach
- Confirm that reporting accurately tracks SLA performance


Channel-specific support:


- If you support customers via Slack, test the full Slack workflow end-to-end
- For Teams, verify the native experience from the customer’s perspective
- Check that all channels feed into unified views


Knowledge base integration:


- Create test articles and evaluate the authoring experience
- Test search functionality with actual customer queries
- Verify that your team can easily share articles during support conversations
- Check analytics to make sure you can identify content gaps


### Step 4: Involve Your Entire Team


A support platform touches multiple teams. Involve teammates from:


- **Support** (Will they actually enjoy using this tool every day? Will leadership get the reporting and oversight they need?)
- **Customer success** (Can they access the account information they need?)
- **Engineering** (How smooth are integration and escalation workflows?)
- **Security** (Does it meet security and compliance requirements?)


The best platform is one that all teams will actually adopt.


### Step 5: Calculate Total Cost of Ownership


Don't just compare contract costs. Factor in the complete investment:


Direct costs:


- Per-seat licensing fees (project for 12-18 months of growth)
- Setup and implementation fees
- Data migration costs
- Integration development or third-party connector costs


Indirect costs:


- Time invested in implementation and configuration
- Productivity loss during transition period
- Ongoing maintenance and administration time
- Cost of feature gaps that require workarounds


Long-term value:


- Projected efficiency gains (tickets resolved per support team member, resolution time improvement)
- Expected retention improvement from better support
- Revenue impact from improved customer satisfaction


### Step 6: Trial the Product


Before committing to a long-term contract, do a trial of the product:


Trial structure:


- Select a subset of your team to test the product
- Trial the platform for 4-6 weeks minimum
- Migrate a representative sample of customer accounts
- Use the platform for all support interactions with trial accounts
- Track specific success metrics (response time, resolution time, support team satisfaction, customer satisfaction)


What to measure:


- Your team’s adoption and satisfaction scores
- Time to competency for new users
- Customer feedback on the support experience
- Technical performance and reliability
- Quality of vendor support during implementation


A successful trial gives you confidence in the platform and leverage to negotiate better terms.


## Common Mistakes to Avoid


### 1. Choosing Based on Brand Recognition


Well-known enterprise platforms aren't always the best fit, especially for growing B2B companies. Large legacy systems often prioritize features you don't always need while lacking the modern communication channel support that B2B customers expect.


Evaluate platforms based on your actual requirements, not market presence.


### 2. Ignoring Your Support Team’s Experience


If your team finds the product clunky and slow, they'll have to find inconvenient workarounds. When you’re evaluating platforms, watch how long it takes to complete common tasks:


- Opening an issue and seeing full context
- Responding to a customer question
- Escalating an issue to another team
- Searching the knowledge base


### 3. Underestimating Implementation Complexity


Some platforms promise quick setup but require extensive configuration, data migration, and integration work. Be realistic about:


- Your team's technical capacity
- Available time for implementation
- Complexity of migrating from your current system
- Learning curve for your team


If you need to be operational quickly, choose a platform with proven fast implementation and strong customer support.


### 4. Overlooking Integration Depth


A platform might claim to integrate with your CRM or communication tools, but shallow integrations create more work than they save. Consider:


- Can your support team see CRM data without leaving the platform?
- Does the integration sync bidirectionally in real-time?
- Can workflows trigger automatically based on integration data?
- How much manual configuration is required?


### 5. Sacrificing Security for Features


Don't compromise on security and compliance, even if it means sacrificing some features. One security breach or compliance violation can cost far more than the difference between platforms.


Make sure any product you consider meets your industry's minimum standards before evaluating its features.


## Making the Final Decision


After thorough evaluation, use this framework to make your final decision:


### Create a Weighted Scorecard


Not all features matter equally. Assign weights to different criteria based on your priorities:


Example weighting:


- Account management capabilities: 25%
- Communication channel support: 20%
- Support team experience: 15%
- Integration ecosystem: 15%
- Pricing: 10%
- Vendor support: 10%
- Security and compliance: 5%


Score each platform against your criteria and calculate weighted totals. This gives you a standardized framework for comparing products.


### Consider Your Growth Trajectory


Choose a platform that fits your needs today and where you'll be in 18-24 months:


- Will the platform scale to your projected issue volume and team size?
- Does it support expansion into new communication channels?
- Can it handle more complex account structures as you move upmarket?
- Will you outgrow the platform's capabilities before the contract ends?


### Evaluate Vendor Partnership Potential


You're not just buying software—you're entering a relationship with a vendor. Assess:


- How responsive has the sales process been?
- What do existing customers say about support quality?
- Is the company investing in product development?
- Do they understand your industry and use case?
- Will you be a meaningful customer to them, or just another contract?


### Negotiate Terms


Once you've selected a platform, negotiate favorable terms:


- Multi-year discounts in exchange for longer commitment
- Flexible contracts that accommodate rapid growth
- Implementation support included in the contract
- Feature development roadmap


### Plan for Change Management


Even the best platform will fail if your team doesn't adopt it. Develop a change management plan:


- Identify champions who will advocate for the new platform
- Create training programs tailored to different roles
- Develop documentation for common workflows
- Set realistic adoption timelines
- Celebrate early wins to build momentum


## The Future of B2B Support Platforms


Understanding emerging trends helps you choose a platform positioned for the future:


### AI Evolution


AI capabilities will continue to help teams scale their support operations:


- Fully autonomous resolution of routine issues
- Predictive routing that considers not issue type, support team expertise, and workload
- Real-time suggestions for support teams during complex interactions
- Automatic generation of knowledge base articles from resolved tickets


### Unified Customer Data Platforms


Support platforms will become central hubs for customer data, integrating signals from:


- Product usage analytics
- Support interactions
- Sales and marketing touchpoints
- Customer success activities
- Financial systems


This unified view will help teams provide truly proactive support that anticipates customer needs before a ticket gets filed.


### Collaborative Customer Spaces


The future of B2B support moves beyond ticketing to shared spaces where customers and support teams collaborate continuously:


- Persistent channels for ongoing relationships
- Shared workspaces for complex implementations
- Visibility into issue resolution progress


This mirrors how B2B relationships actually work: as ongoing partnerships rather than discrete transactions.


### Industry-Specific Specialization


Expect platforms to develop deeper specialization for specific industries:


- Healthcare with HIPAA compliance built-in
- Financial services with SOC 2 and regulatory reporting
- Manufacturing with equipment lifecycle tracking
- SaaS with usage-based support models


Generic platforms will struggle to compete with specialized solutions that understand industry-specific workflows and compliance requirements.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What's the difference between B2B and B2C support platforms?


B2B support platforms organize around accounts with multiple stakeholders, handle longer resolution cycles, and integrate with business communication channels like Slack and Teams. B2C platforms focus on high-volume, quick-resolution tickets from individual consumers. B2B platforms also provide deeper account health insights, contract management, and SLA tracking capabilities that B2C platforms typically lack.


### How do B2B support systems manage multiple products under one account?


Modern B2B platforms use hierarchical account structures that let you organize multiple products, service tiers, or business lines under a single customer account. They provide product-specific tagging, specialized routing to expert teams, separate SLA tracking per product, and segmented reporting. This ensures support teams have the right context and expertise while maintaining unified visibility across the entire relationship.


### Why is native Slack or Teams integration important for B2B support?


B2B customers spend their workday in business communication platforms. Forcing them to switch to email or web portals creates friction. Native integration means customers can raise, discuss, and resolve issues entirely within Slack or Teams while your team gets full ticketing capabilities behind the scenes. This improves response times, customer satisfaction, and adoption rates.[Learn more about using Slack as a ticketing system](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/slack-as-a-ticketing-system-2025) .


### What are the most important metrics for B2B support platforms?


Beyond basic ticket volume and response time, B2B platforms should track account health scores, SLA compliance rates, customer satisfaction (CSAT) by account tier, time to resolution segmented by issue type, support's impact on renewal rates, and cost per ticket. The best platforms correlate support metrics with business outcomes like retention and expansion revenue.


### How much should I budget for a B2B support platform?


Pricing varies dramatically from $25-$200+ per seat per month depending on features, integrations, and scale. Factor in implementation costs (typically 10-30% of annual license costs), data migration, integration development, and training. Research shows that modern customer service platforms deliver 315% ROI over three years with less than 6-month payback periods, making the investment highly worthwhile for B2B companies.


### Can I use Microsoft Teams as a helpdesk platform?


Teams can serve as a communication channel for support, but it lacks purpose-built ticketing, SLA management, and reporting capabilities. Most companies use Teams together with a dedicated support platform that has a native Teams integration. This gives customers the convenience of Teams-based communication while giving your team proper support tools.[Read our guide on Microsoft Teams helpdesk solutions](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/microsoft-teams-helpdesk-2025-guide) .


### How long does it take to implement a B2B support platform?


Implementation timelines range from 1-2 weeks for simple platforms to 3-6 months for complex enterprise systems. Factors affecting timeline include data migration complexity, number of integrations required, customization needs, team size, and vendor implementation support. Plan for at least 4-6 weeks even with fast-to-deploy platforms to ensure proper configuration, testing, and training.


### What security certifications should a B2B support platform have?


At minimum, look for SOC 2 Type II compliance and GDPR compliance. Industry-specific certifications matter too: HIPAA for healthcare, PCI DSS for payment processing, FedRAMP for government contracts. Also verify role-based access controls, data encryption, SSO support, and comprehensive audit logging. Don't compromise on security—one breach can cost a lot more than platform differences.


### How does AI improve B2B support platforms?


AI enhances B2B support through automatic ticket triage and routing, response suggestions that your support team can edit and send, sentiment analysis to flag at-risk accounts, conversation summarization, knowledge base article recommendations, and predictive account health scoring. 92% of CRM leaders report AI has improved response times, and adoption continues accelerating as AI becomes more sophisticated.


### Should I choose a specialized B2B platform or adapt a general support tool?


Specialized B2B platforms understand the unique requirements of business customer support: account hierarchies, multi-stakeholder management, business messaging integration, and complex SLAs. General tools adapted for B2B often require extensive customization and lack purpose-built features. Unless you have significant technical resources for customization, platforms that are built for B2B provide faster time to value.


## Conclusion


Choosing a B2B support platform is one of the most important operational decisions you'll make. The right platform becomes invisible to your customers while empowering your team to deliver exceptional support. The wrong one creates frustration for both customers and your team, ultimately harming retention and revenue.


Focus on platforms that are purpose-built for B2B:


- Account-centric architecture that manages relationships, not just tickets
- Native integration with business communication channels like Slack, Teams, and Discord
- Deep insights into account health that help you provide proactive support
- Seamless collaboration between support, customer success, and product teams
- AI that boosts your team rather than attempting to replace them


Start with a clear understanding of your requirements, test platforms with real scenarios, involve your entire team in the decision, and run a trial before committing. The investment in a thorough evaluation process pays dividends in successful implementation and long-term satisfaction.
